The module contract

Source: CONTRACT.md

A module is a function or object the package runs through a registry: an extractor, cleaner, segmenter, reader, embedder, protocol or step, or a module of your own. The module contract is what the core requires of a module and what a conformance check reports about it. Its version is what hr_contract_version() returns (internal, in R/core-registry-contract.R):

Current version: 0.2

What the version covers

  1. Kinds of module. A layer tells the core about a kind with hr_register_kind(name, ...). The core keeps name and whatever else is given (the document layer gives registry, the name of the registry its modules are kept in). The document layer registers six kinds at load: extractor, cleaner, segmenter, reader, embedder and protocol. The core then registers its own kind, step, whose registry it keeps itself. Models are not a kind: the model registry stays outside the module registry.
  2. The entry fields. An entry registered with hr_register() has version and contract: the version you give (for a step, the step’s own version when you give none) and the contract version the package implements. An entry registered through a kind’s own function, such as gr_register_reader(), has neither, and every listing shows NA for it; its conformance check stays advisory. Each listing (gr_readers(), gr_segmenters(), gr_cleaners(), gr_extractors(), gr_embedders(), gr_protocols() and hr_modules()) shows them as its last two columns, version then contract, and keeps its other columns, their types, their order and its row names.
  3. The conformance report. hr_check_module(fn, run, rules, kind, name) returns an hr_conformance data frame with the columns rule, ok (TRUE, FALSE, or NA for a rule not checked) and detail (one string, "" when there is nothing to say), and the attributes kind, name, contract (this version) and warnings. The first two rows are always is_function and runs. A rule returns TRUE, FALSE or NA, or a list with ok and detail.
  4. The reader rules (gr_check_reader()): answer_class, answer_fields (the answer has answer, reader, question, chunks_used, partial, notes, trace, warnings and signature, and partial is one TRUE or FALSE), answer_text, evidence, chunks_used, calls_declared and calls_within_cost.
  5. The segmenter rules (gr_check_segmenter()): chunks_class, chunk_columns (chunk_id, text, tokens, chars, page, section and block_id), chunk_text, chunk_ids, within_cap and calls_declared.
  6. The rules for the other kinds (internal; the conformance tests run them on every registered module): extractor blocks_shape, block_text, block_columns, unread_pages; cleaner text_class, keeps_text, logged, deterministic; embedder matrix_shape, finite, unit_rows, source, deterministic; protocol protocol_class, name_matches, question, criteria, fields, outline, round_trip; step returns_value, declared_output, held_attached; and, for a reader under a call cap, within_max_calls, stops_cleanly, partial_when_capped.

The version is recorded where a result depends on it: in the contract attribute of every conformance report, and in the contract field of each module registered with hr_register().

Signal calibrations keep a contract of their own. The contract_version field of a calibration key (hr_calibrate_signal()) is filled with the signal contract version when the key leaves it out, and that version stays at 0.1 (internal, .hr_signal_contract in R/core-signal-calibrate.R). A record you saved under 0.1 stays valid, and its key stays byte-identical, when the module contract moves.

Rules for changing it

  • Any change to the fields above (a kind added or removed, a column or attribute of the report, a rule added, removed, renamed or made stricter) bumps the minor version: 0.1 to 0.2. A change that touches none of them, such as a clearer detail message, does not.
  • Each bump gets an entry below that lists every field that changed.
  • The version is pinned in tests/testthat/test-core-kinds.R, and tests/testthat/test-contract-files.R checks that the current version at the top of this file is the one hr_contract_version() returns. Change all three together.
  • Once the conformance checks have passed for two releases in a row, the fields are frozen, and 1.0 follows.

Changelog

0.2 (2026-11-24)

  • Kinds: protocol (registry protocols) and step (registry steps, kept by the core) join the five kinds of 0.1. hr_register() and hr_modules() cover both, and each kind has a conformance check.
  • Entry fields: version and contract, NA for an entry registered through a kind’s own function.
  • Listings: the six gr_*() listings and hr_modules() end with version and contract. No other column changed.
  • Signal calibrations: their contract_version default is the signal contract, frozen at 0.1, instead of this version.
  • Rules: the extractor, cleaner, embedder, protocol, step and call cap rules listed above, added on 2026-11-24 without a bump, now belong to the contract.
  • The conformance report, the reader rules and the segmenter rules are unchanged; a report’s contract attribute now says 0.2.

Earlier changes under 0.1

No field changes; the version stays 0.1. Checked on 2026-11-22 against the commit that added the conformance checks (b40139e): hr_check_module(), the report, hr_register_kind() and the reader and segmenter rules are unchanged since. The calibration key started recording contract_version in this period; that records the version and does not change the contract.

0.1 (2026-11-05)

The first version, with the core’s own state and registry of kinds (2184208). The conformance report and the reader and segmenter rules followed on 2026-11-06 (b40139e), under the same version. All fields above as listed.
